I am to predict the churn from the data

Churn rate is a measure of the number of customers or employees who leave a company during a given period. It can also refer to the amount of revenue lost as a result of the departures. Changes in a business's churn rate can provide valuable insight into an organization.

Don’t forget that you need to first do the analysis to understand the data before modeling

#num_cols = X.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns
num_cols = X_1.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns

for col in num_cols:
    Q1 = X_1[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = X_1[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1

    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

    # Winsorization (cap values to bounds)
    X_1[col] = X_1[col].clip(lower=lower_bound, upper=upper_bound) # applying winsorization to the numerical columns

# 1) Define columns
cat_cols = [ 'Geography' ,'Gender']

num_cols = [col for col in X_1.columns if col not in cat_cols + ['Target']]
# encoding the categorical columns
ord_enc = OrdinalEncoder(handle_unknown='use_encoded_value', unknown_value=-1)

X_1[cat_cols] = ord_enc.fit_transform(X_1[cat_cols])

# 3) Scaler for numeric
scaler = StandardScaler()

# 4) Compose transformer
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ('target_enc', TargetEncoder(), cat_cols),
        ('scale', scaler, num_cols)
    ],
    remainder='drop'  # drop any other cols, if present
)

# 5) Fit & transform
df_transformed = preprocessor.fit_transform(X_1, y)

# If transform returns numpy array, convert back to DataFrame
import pandas as pd
encoded_cols = cat_cols + num_cols
df_transformed = pd.DataFrame(df_transformed, columns=encoded_cols)
print(df_transformed.shape)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, StratifiedKFold, cross_validate
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler  # Logistic Regression benefits from scaling!
from sklearn.metrics import (
    classification_report, confusion_matrix,
    precision_recall_curve, auc, make_scorer
)
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Assume X (features) and y (target Series, where y = df['Target'])
# If y is a DataFrame: y = y.squeeze() or y = y['Target']

# 1. Train/test split (stratified)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42
)

# Define scoring metrics (F1 and PR-AUC are key for imbalance)
scoring = {
    'f1': 'f1',
    'precision': 'precision',
    'recall': 'recall',
    'pr_auc': make_scorer(
        lambda y_true, y_proba: auc(*precision_recall_curve(y_true, y_proba)[:2]),
        needs_proba=True
    )
}
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)


# # -----------------------------
# OPTION 2: SMOTE + Logistic Regression
# -----------------------------
print("\n" + "="*60)
print("Evaluating: SMOTE + Logistic Regression")

lr_smote = Pipeline([
    ('smote', SMOTE(random_state=42)),
    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
    ('classifier', LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000))
])

cv_smote = cross_validate(lr_smote, X_train, y_train, cv=cv, scoring=scoring, n_jobs=-1)

print("CV Results (SMOTE):")
for metric in ['f1', 'precision', 'recall', 'pr_auc']:
    mean = cv_smote[f'test_{metric}'].mean()
    std = cv_smote[f'test_{metric}'].std()
    print(f"  {metric.upper()}: {mean:.4f} ± {std:.4f}")

lr_smote.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred_s = lr_smote.predict(X_test)
y_proba_s = lr_smote.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

print("\n Test Set (SMOTE):")
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_s, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

# -----------------------------
# Compare PR Curves (Optional but insightful)
# -----------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))

# Weighted
prec_w, rec_w, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test, y_proba_w)
pr_auc_w = auc(rec_w, prec_w)
plt.plot(rec_w, prec_w, label=f'Class Weighting (PR-AUC = {pr_auc_w:.3f})')

# SMOTE
prec_s, rec_s, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test, y_proba_s)
pr_auc_s = auc(rec_s, prec_s)
plt.plot(rec_s, prec_s, label=f'SMOTE (PR-AUC = {pr_auc_s:.3f})')

# Baseline (no skill classifier)
no_skill = len(y_test[y_test == 1]) / len(y_test)
plt.axhline(no_skill, color='gray', linestyle='--', label=f'No Skill ({no_skill:.3f})')

plt.xlabel('Recall')
plt.ylabel('Precision')
plt.title('Precision-Recall Curves: Logistic Regression (Imbalanced Data)')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, StratifiedKFold, GridSearchCV
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, f1_score
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")  # to suppress convergence warnings during search

# Assume X (features), y (target: Series with 0/1)

# 1. Train/test split (keep test set untouched)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42
)

# 2. Define cross-validation strategy (stratified, 5 folds)
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

# OPTION B: Tune with SMOTE (Alternative)
print("\n" + "="*60)
print("Tuning Logistic Regression with SMOTE...")

pipeline_smote = Pipeline([
    ('smote', SMOTE(random_state=42)),
    ('scaler', StandardScaler()),
    ('classifier', LogisticRegression(
        random_state=42,
        max_iter=1000,
        solver='liblinear'
    ))
])

param_grid_smote = {
    'classifier__C': [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100],
    'classifier__penalty': ['l1', 'l2']
}

grid_smote = GridSearchCV(
    pipeline_smote,
    param_grid_smote,
    cv=cv,
    scoring='f1',
    n_jobs=-1,
    verbose=1
)

grid_smote.fit(X_train, y_train)
print("Best params (SMOTE):", grid_smote.best_params_)
print("Best CV F1-score:", grid_smote.best_score_)

y_pred_s = grid_smote.predict(X_test)
print("\nTest Results (SMOTE):")
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred_s, target_names=['Class 0', 'Class 1']))

============================================================
Tuning Logistic Regression with SMOTE...
Fitting 5 folds for each of 10 candidates, totalling 50 fits

Best CV F1-score: 0.5026297565189335

Test Results (SMOTE):

     Class 0       0.90      0.73      0.81      1593
     Class 1       0.40      0.70      0.51       407

    accuracy                           0.72      2000

weighted avg       0.80      0.72      0.75      2000
